qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Entrenched Irish banking duopoly (alongside AIB) controlling over 70% of domestic deposits and lending following foreign bank exits. Protected by sticky retail deposit relationships and primary transaction accounts, though lending products lack pricing power over monetary cycles.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Dominant Irish banking duopoly franchise with AIB; RoTE ~17% in 2023-2024 supported by foreign bank exits and high ECB rates. However, spread-lending earnings have peaked and are declining with ECB rate cuts, while facing aggressive fintech competition from Revolut and high Irish regulatory/political scrutiny.
qualitative.evidence: FY24 adjusted RoTE was 16.8% with PBT of €1.85B and NII of €3,565M (down 3% from €3,682M in FY23 as ECB rates peaked and began easing). While structural hedging and duopoly deposit market share protect near-term margins, commercial fractional-reserve spread-lenders lack 15-year secular persistence.
